summary: A correlated subquery refers to the current row of the outer query, so it runs once for each row.
points: It connects through a table alias: WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees x WHERE x.department_id = e.department_id).
Use it to compare each row with its own group.
It can run slowly on very large tables, as it repeats per row.

example.explanation: Each employee is compared with the average of their own department.
